mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal or stagnation of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained positive change in WORKPLACES mobility for at least three consecutive weeks signifies a broader return to office work and associated weekday spending, directly boosting RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES shows a positive change week-on-week for at least 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES showing consistent week-on-week increases.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a general increase in out-of-home activity for essential needs, which will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation as confidence grows over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 28 days, even as RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall and GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: As public health policies allow for greater movement, the observed recovery in TRANSIT station visits indicates increased comfort with public transport, which facilitates access to retail and recreation areas, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite a continued upward trend in TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility, indicating increased outdoor leisure activity, will translate into higher RETAIL_REC as people extend their outings to include shopping and dining within the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 1.0 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 7 days, despite the observed week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The combined upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signifies a return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns, which inherently increases exposure and access to retail and recreation opportunities, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, even with concurrent increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and accelerating recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, representing essential out-of-home activity, acts as a leading indicator for increased general comfort and willingness to engage in non-essential retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a sustained shift away from staying at home, reflecting increased willingness to venture out for various activities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, assuming no new restrictions are imposed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline.
